questions.q: Why do subscription services appeal to customers, according to Tzuo?
a: They give access to a service without the work of owning anything
They are always cheaper than buying a product once
They let customers own the latest version outright
They remove the need for any customer support
questions.why: Lesson 1 says people want the music or transport, not the CD or car they would have to maintain.

questions.q: What share of the 1955 Fortune 500 was still on the list when Tzuo wrote?
a: About 12%
About 30%
About half
About 60%
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the 12% survival rate to show how few companies adapt to changing customer needs.

questions.q: How does the subscription approach to innovation differ from the old one?
a: It starts with what customers want and keeps changing after release
It perfects the product fully before anyone sees it
It moves in order through research, design and manufacturing
It relies on one large launch each year
questions.why: Lesson 2 says subscription businesses release early and adjust constantly using customer feedback.

questions.q: What does the D in the PADRE method stand for?
a: Deploy, getting customers set up quickly and painlessly
Design, shaping the product around customer needs
Develop, building new features on a fixed schedule
Distribute, shipping the product out to retailers
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists deploy as the step where the customer is set up fast enough to stay interested.

questions.q: What three areas does the PPM checklist cover?
a: People, product and money
Pipeline, product and marketing
Price, promotion and market share
People, process and metrics
questions.why: Lesson 3 says PPM means top talent, constant product improvement and well-divided resources.
